item.description:
Xander is an Assistant Professor (UK Lecturer) in Global Terrestrial Water in the School of Geographical and Earth Sciences at the university of glasgow. He is also an Affiliate Lecturer in the James Watt School of Engineering.

He is a visiting research collaborator at the High Meadows Environmental Institute at princeton university, and an associate with the stockholm resilience centre.

ExaGEO PhD project: From roots to rainfall: modelling climate interactions and vulnerability of groundwater-dependent ecosystems

Funding: NERC ExaGEO Doctoral Landscape Award studentship (competitive)
Project institution: University of Glasgow
Supervisors: Dr Xander Huggins (University of Glasgow, principal supervisor), Dr Wenxin Zhang (University of Glasgow), Dr Nick A Chappell (Lancaster University), and Dr Dave McKay (University of Edinburgh)

This PhD will study how groundwater-dependent ecosystems in drylands connect groundwater, vegetation, and the atmosphere. It will use GPU-accelerated modelling and atmospheric moisture tracking to test how these ecosystems respond to falling groundwater, and which of them contribute most to regional rainfall and to ecosystems downwind.

Funded PhD studentship: What role does groundwater play in social-ecological regime shifts?

Funding: fully funded, 3 years
Start: flexible, no later than October 2027
Location: School of Geographical and Earth Sciences, University of Glasgow
Apply: expression of interest form, reviewed on a rolling basis until 31 January 2027

context

Groundwater is among the least studied aspects of social-ecological systems. This is partly because it is a slow variable in these systems, partly because it is invisible beneath our feet, and partly because groundwater researchers only make up a small contingent of the social-ecological systems community. Yet groundwater is closely connected to many human, environmental and Earth system processes (Huggins et al. 2023; Gleeson et al. 2020). Many of these processes behave non-linearly, and some may meet the definition of a regime shift (a large, persistent change in how a system is structured and how it functions). Despite sustained efforts to catalogue social-ecological regime shifts (Rocha et al. 2015) and to build middle-range theories of land system change (Meyfroidt et al. 2018), groundwater’s role remains underrepresented and thus largely unknown in these contexts.

IAPETUS PhD project: Finding and protecting Scotland’s hidden groundwater-dependent ecosystems

Funding: NERC IAPETUS doctoral training partnership studentship (competitive), studentship ID IAP-26-044
Lead institution: University of Glasgow, School of Geographical and Earth Sciences
Supervisors: Dr Xander Huggins (University of Glasgow), Donald John MacAllister and Sarah Collins (British Geological Survey)

This PhD will produce the first comprehensive map of groundwater-dependent ecosystems in Scotland, and improve methods to detect them in humid, energy-limited landscapes. It will map the groundwatersheds of these ecosystems to assess cumulative risks from land use, contamination, warming, and drought, and examine how the ecosystems may change under future land use, water use, and climate scenarios. The project includes training and placement time at the British Geological Survey in Edinburgh.

finding your own funding for a PhD

These programmes fund PhD students every year. If you think one of these fits you, please be in touch with me well before the deadline because most need a supervisor’s support when you apply.

  • College of Science and Engineering Graduate School Scholarship (University of Glasgow). Covers full tuition fees and a stipend at the UKRI rate, in any research area of the College. You need a supervisor’s support before you apply. Applications are due by 31 January. [details]
  • DiveIn Centre for Doctoral Training (EPSRC, University of Glasgow). A fully funded, four-year interdisciplinary PhD programme. Students join a cohort without a set project, and form their project and supervisory team during the programme. Our work fits best with its Planetary Health research area. [details]
  • IAPETUS and ExaGEO (NERC doctoral training programmes). Both run a studentship competition every year, with new projects posted each autumn. [IAPETUS] | [ExaGEO]
  • James McCune Smith PhD Scholarships (University of Glasgow). For Black UK-domiciled students, in any discipline. [details]
  • China Scholarship Council scholarships.

I also welcome MSc by Research students.

here are some scientific outreach initiatives I have participated in and/or led

  • Panel member in UVic Water Research and the SDGs: A Panel Discussion (2022). Watch the panel discussion here.

  • Participating scientist in the inaugural Water Day on the Hill (2020). An event that brought together water scientists across Canada to meet with parliamentarians and senior federal officials to raise awareness around water security in Canada. Read the report about the day of activities here.

  • Circle of Blue (2020). Perspective: How does the coronavirus pandemic compare to the global groundwater crisis? Read the thought-piece here.

  • Water availability stripes. Access the data visualisation here. A science communication tool and fun data-vis project to bring awareness to recent trends in water availability around the world.

  • Managing editor (2016-2021) of the Water Underground blog. Water Underground is a global collective of hydrogeologic researchers for water resource professionals, academics and anyone interested in groundwater, research, teaching and supervision. The blog is hosted on both the EGU Blogs and the AGU blogospheres. Read the blog here.

Our mission is to use interdisciplinary, data-driven approaches to study groundwater and freshwater interactions with social-ecological and human-Earth systems with the goal of generating process-based insights to support groundwater sustainability, ecological integrity, social well-being and justice, inclusive development, and Earth system resilience through improved water management, policy, advocacy, and education.

curriculum development

I have co-developed a set of resources to support teaching sustainability, equity, and anti-racism in undergraduate civil engineering curriculum. These resources are available on the “Learn and Teach Green, People-Centered Civil Engeering website (website geo-restricted to Canada, contact me for access while we work to remove the institutional geo-restriction).
